share.def: A unit of ownership in a company. Owning one share makes you a part-owner of the business, its assets, and its profits, in proportion to the total shares issued.

dhitopatra.def: The legal umbrella term for shares, debentures and bonds — anything SEBON regulates as a tradeable financial instrument.

kitta.def: One share. NEPSE quantities are always expressed in kitta; the usual minimum order is 10.

lagani.def: Money committed to an asset in the expectation of a return. In Nepali market usage it usually implies a holding period longer than a trade.

promoter_share.def: Shares held by the founders of a company. They carry lock-in periods, trade in a separate market at a different price, and can only be converted to public shares under SEBON rules.

public_share.def: The ordinary shares held by the investing public and traded freely on NEPSE. This is what you buy.

paid_up_capital.def: The total money shareholders have actually paid into the company for its shares — share count × face value. Nepal Rastra Bank sets minimums for banks.

primary_market.def: Where shares are issued by the company for the first time — an IPO, FPO or rights issue. Your money goes to the company.

secondary_market.def: Where existing shares change hands between investors on NEPSE. Your money goes to the seller, not the company.

face_value.def: The nominal accounting value printed on a share — Rs. 100 for ordinary Nepali shares, Rs. 10 for mutual fund units. It is not what the share is worth.

market_price.def: What the last buyer and seller agreed on. An opinion, updated continuously, not a measurement of value.

book_value.def: Net assets divided by shares outstanding — what the accounts say each share is backed by. Arithmetic, unlike market price.

nepse.def: Nepal Stock Exchange. The single exchange operating Nepal's secondary equity market; opened its trading floor in January 1994.

sebon.def: Securities Board of Nepal, the regulator. It licenses issuers and brokers, approves prospectuses, and is where you file a complaint.

cdsc.def: CDS and Clearing Ltd — the central depository that holds every dematerialised share in Nepal and runs MeroShare.

dp.def: The institution — usually a bank or broker — that holds your Demat account on CDSC's behalf and charges you the Rs. 25 per-settlement DP fee.

rta.def: The firm that manages a company's shareholder register and runs the IPO allotment lottery.

broker.def: A NEPSE-licensed firm through which all orders must be routed. Brokers are numbered, and their numbers appear on the floorsheet.

sectoral_index.def: One of 13 sub-indices tracking a group of companies — Commercial Banks, Hydropower, Microfinance and so on.

sensitive_index.def: A NEPSE sub-index covering only Group A companies — the larger, better-disclosed names. Moves less than the headline index.

float_index.def: An index weighted only by shares actually available to trade, excluding promoter and locked-in holdings.

market_cap.def: Share price × total shares outstanding. NEPSE's total stood at Rs. 4.547 trillion on 15 August 2026.

pre_open.def: A session before continuous trading in which orders are collected without matching and one opening price is calculated. Band is ±5% of previous close since 2026.

demat.def: The electronic account, held with a DP under CDSC, in which your shares actually live. Required before you can apply for any IPO.

meroshare.def: CDSC's web portal for custody: your holdings, your WACC, IPO applications through My ASBA, and EDIS authorisation. It cannot place trades.

tms.def: The web platform, provided through your broker, where you actually place buy and sell orders. It is not your portfolio of record.

connectips.def: Nepal's interbank payment rail, used to move money from your bank into your broker's collection account and to block funds for an IPO.

ltp.def: The price at which the most recent trade executed. The ±3% order band is measured from this, not from the previous close.

previous_close.def: Yesterday's closing price. The ±15% daily circuit is measured from this figure.

bid.def: The highest price a buyer is currently willing to pay. You sell into the bid.

ask.def: The lowest price a seller is currently willing to accept. You buy at the ask.

spread.def: The gap between best bid and best ask. On thin NEPSE counters it can reach 2–3% and dwarf your commission — it is your first and largest cost.

volume.def: The number of shares traded in a period. Measured in kitta, not rupees.

turnover.def: The rupee value of shares traded — price × volume. NEPSE's daily average was Rs. 3.68 billion in the week to 15 August 2026.

floorsheet.def: NEPSE's published record of every executed trade: buying broker, selling broker, quantity and rate. Public, and the rawest data the exchange gives you.

limit_order.def: An order with a named maximum buying price or minimum selling price. On NEPSE this is the only order type that exists.

market_order.def: An order to trade at whatever price is available. Not offered on NEPSE — every order must name a price.

price_time_priority.def: The matching rule: better prices fill first, and among equal prices the order that arrived earliest fills first.

order_book.def: The list of your live, pending, partially filled and cancelled orders. Not the same as the trade book.

trade_book.def: The list of your actually executed trades. An order appears here only once it has filled.

partial_fill.def: When only part of your quantity finds a counterparty. The remainder stays live. A fill split across two days costs you two DP charges.

circuit.def: The maximum a single stock may move in one day — ±15% of previous close since 21 April 2026, raised from ±10%.

order_band.def: The window around the last traded price within which an order may be placed — ±3% during continuous trading. Separate from, and tighter than, the daily circuit.

circuit_breaker.def: A market-wide halt. Since April 2026: ±5% within the first two hours halts trading 15 minutes; ±8% at any time closes the market for the day.

settlement.def: The exchange of shares for money that completes a trade. NEPSE settles T+2, counted in trading days.

t_plus_two.def: Trade day plus two trading days. A Thursday sale settles the following Monday; weekends and holidays extend it.

edis.def: The authorisation you submit in MeroShare on T+1 to release sold shares from your Demat account. Without it, the sale fails.

auction_settlement.def: What happens when a seller fails to deliver: NEPSE buys the shares in the market to give to the buyer, and charges the difference plus a penalty to the defaulting seller.

intraday.def: Buying and selling the same share within one day. Structurally impossible on NEPSE, because you cannot sell shares that have not yet settled into your Demat.

commission.def: A regulated five-slab charge from 0.36% down to 0.24%, applied to the whole transaction value on both the buy and the sell leg.

sebon_fee.def: A regulatory levy of 0.015% of transaction value on equity trades (0.010% corporate debentures, 0.005% government bonds).

dp_charge.def: A flat Rs. 25, levied per company per settlement date — not per trade. Being flat, it is punishing on small trades.

cgt.def: Tax on your profit, withheld at source during settlement. Since 17 July 2026: individuals 10% at ≤365 days, 7.5% above; institutions 10%.

final_tax.def: A tax settled at source that you do not declare or pay again in your annual return. Nepali CGT on listed shares works this way — which also means losses cannot offset other income.

wacc.def: Your average per-share purchase cost across all lots, shown in MeroShare. It is the cost basis used to compute your capital gains tax.

break_even.def: The selling price at which you neither gain nor lose, after round-trip commission, SEBON fee and two DP charges.

round_trip.def: Everything you pay to enter and exit one position. Keeping it under about 1% requires positions of roughly Rs. 25,000 or more.

ipo.def: A company's first sale of shares to the public, at Rs. 100 face value for fixed-price issues, minimum 10 units.

casba.def: Centralised Application Supported by Blocked Amount. Your IPO money is blocked in your own bank account, not debited, until allotment.

book_building.def: A price-discovery IPO method for larger issuers. Minimum 50 units for retail, who receive a 10% discount to the institutional price.

allotment.def: The computerised lottery that decides who receives shares in an oversubscribed issue. Every valid application has equal probability regardless of size.

fpo.def: An additional share issue by a company already listed, usually priced at a premium to face value.

hakprad.def: An offer to existing shareholders to buy additional shares at a set price, in proportion to their holding. Unexercised rights simply lapse.

bonus_share.def: Extra shares issued free to existing holders from reserves. Not new value — your share count rises, the price adjusts down, and your WACC falls.

stock_split.def: Dividing existing shares into more, smaller units. Purely cosmetic: the same company value across more pieces.

mutual_fund.def: A pooled fund listed on NEPSE with Rs. 10 face value and a fixed maturity. Units routinely trade below NAV.

nav.def: The per-unit value of a fund's holdings, published monthly. The market price of a closed-end unit is usually lower.

candle.def: A chart mark encoding four numbers for one period: open, high, low and close. The body is the settled result; the wicks are ground taken and given back.

body.def: The distance between open and close — the net result of the session.

wick.def: The thin line from the body to the high or the low. It marks price that was reached and then given back.

doji_term.def: A candle whose open and close are effectively equal. It records indecision, not reversal.

marubozu.def: A candle that is almost all body with negligible wicks — one side controlled the entire session.

engulfing.def: A two-candle reversal where the second body completely covers the first. Only bodies need to be engulfed, not wicks.

trend.def: A sequence of higher highs and higher lows (up) or lower highs and lower lows (down). Anything else is a range.

support.def: A price level where buying has repeatedly stopped a decline. Its strength comes from the number of times it has held.

resistance.def: A price level where selling has repeatedly stopped an advance.

breakout.def: Price closing decisively beyond a support or resistance level. Without volume confirmation it is more often a fakeout.

liquidity_trap.def: A NEPSE-specific hazard: a valid technical signal on a counter so thin you cannot buy or sell meaningful size at the signalled price.

sma.def: The average close over the last N periods, recomputed each period. Common settings on NEPSE are 20, 50 and 200 days.

ema.def: A moving average that weights recent prices more heavily, so it turns faster than an SMA of the same length.

rsi.def: A 0–100 momentum oscillator comparing average gains to average losses over 14 periods. Overbought is not a sell signal.

macd.def: The difference between a 12- and 26-period EMA, with a 9-period signal line. The histogram shows momentum changing.

divergence.def: When price makes a new extreme but the indicator does not. A warning that the move is losing force, not a trade trigger.

eps.def: Net profit divided by shares outstanding. Bonus issues inflate the denominator, so historical EPS must be restated before comparison.

pe.def: Price divided by EPS. In Nepali banking a very high P/E almost always means collapsed earnings, not priced-in growth. Sector median: 14.92×.

pb.def: Price divided by book value per share. For banks it is often more stable than P/E because book value moves slowly.

roe.def: Net profit as a percentage of shareholders' equity — how efficiently the business turns your capital into earnings. Always read it beside P/E.

roa.def: Net profit as a percentage of total assets. For a bank it strips out the flattering effect of leverage.

nim.def: The spread between what a bank earns on loans and pays on deposits, as a percentage of earning assets. The bank's core profitability.

npl.def: Loans not being repaid, as a percentage of total loans. Rising NPL precedes falling EPS by two to four quarters.

cd_ratio.def: How much of a bank's deposits it has lent out. A stretched CD ratio across the system was the upstream cause of the 2021–2023 crash.

provisioning.def: Money a bank sets aside against loans it expects to lose. Provisions reduce reported profit, which is why Q4 EPS often disappoints.

ddm.def: Valuing a share as the present value of its future dividends. Usable for a mature Nepali bank; meaningless for a pre-COD hydropower project.

plf.def: Actual generation divided by theoretical maximum generation. The number that tells you what a hydropower licence is really worth.

ppa.def: The contract with Nepal Electricity Authority fixing tariff, term and take-or-pay conditions. Without one, a project has no route to revenue.

cod.def: The date a project starts selling power commercially. Before it, any reported EPS is close to meaningless.

run_of_river.def: A hydropower design with no large storage reservoir, so generation follows the river. Most Nepali projects are this, which makes earnings brutally seasonal.

par.def: The microfinance equivalent of NPL — the share of the loan book overdue beyond a threshold, usually 30 days.

claims_ratio.def: Claims paid as a proportion of premiums earned. The core measure of whether an insurer priced its risk correctly.

solvency_margin.def: Capital held above the minimum required to meet expected claims. The regulator's measure of whether an insurer can survive a bad year.

position_size.def: How many kitta you buy. Derived from your stop distance and your rupee risk — never chosen first.

stop_loss.def: The price at which you accept you were wrong and exit. NEPSE has no stop-loss order type — it is a decision you must execute manually.

risk_reward.def: Expected gain divided by the amount risked. At 2:1 you can be wrong 60% of the time and still finish ahead.

drawdown.def: The fall from a peak to a trough in your account or an index. Recovering a loss L requires a gain of L/(1−L).

expectancy.def: (win rate × average win) − (loss rate × average loss). The single number that says whether a system makes money.

correlation.def: How closely two holdings move together. Five Nepali commercial banks are close to one position, not five.

loss_aversion.def: The tendency to feel a loss roughly twice as strongly as an equivalent gain, which is why losers get held and winners get sold.

averaging_down.def: Buying more of a falling position to reduce your WACC. It lowers your average cost and raises your total risk at the same time.

anchoring.def: Letting an irrelevant number — your buy price, or the Rs. 100 face value — govern a decision that should rest on the business.

pump_and_dump.def: Coordinated accumulation, a seeded tip, retail buying, then organisers selling into that demand. Prohibited by SEBON; report it rather than trying to time it.

trade_journal.def: A record of every trade with its thesis, entry, stop, size and outcome. Seven columns are enough; more and you will stop filling it in.

r_multiple.def: A trade's result expressed in units of the amount risked. A trade risking Rs. 6,000 that earns Rs. 12,000 is +2R.
